justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a relatively stable and modest upward drift assumption across all three horizons. At the one-day horizon, I anchored closely to the prevailing price level, assuming mean-reverting intraday behavior with minimal directional conviction — the 206.5 estimate essentially represents a slight continuation of recent momentum with little expected deviation overnight. At the one-week horizon, the 207.0 estimate reflects a nearly flat trajectory, acknowledging that short-term equity or asset price movements tend to be noisy and that any trend signals are weak enough to justify only marginal upward adjustment. At the one-month horizon, the 208.0 estimate incorporates a slightly larger drift premium, consistent with the historically positive expected return on risky assets over multi-week periods, while still remaining conservative given the absence of strong fundamental catalysts.

The confidence interval widths expand appropriately with time horizon, reflecting the square-root-of-time scaling of uncertainty under a random walk framework. At one day, the 12-point range (200.5–212.5) captures typical daily volatility. By one week, the range widens to 22 points, and by one month, it broadens to 44 points (186–230), reflecting the compounding of daily uncertainty over more trading sessions. These widths were also influenced by recent realized volatility, which appears moderate rather than elevated, preventing even wider intervals while still acknowledging that multi-week price paths can diverge substantially from starting conditions.

Several specific risks could push outcomes outside these stated intervals. On the downside, a sudden deterioration in macroeconomic data — such as a sharper-than-expected employment report, renewed inflation surprises, or a credit event in financial markets — could produce sharp selling pressure that breaches the lower bounds, particularly at the one-month horizon. Geopolitical escalation or an unexpected central bank policy shift could similarly amplify volatility beyond what historical norms would suggest. On the upside, a strong earnings season, a dovish policy pivot, or a resolution of an ongoing geopolitical tension could drive prices well above 230 within a month. Tail events, by definition, are difficult to assign probabilities to, and my 90% confidence intervals deliberately leave 10% of probability mass in the tails to acknowledge these scenarios exist and are non-trivial.
